name: Brown's Hotel London
positioning: Rocco Forte's Brown's Hotel in London's Mayfair, welcoming guests since 1832, with a wood-panelled Drawing Room for afternoon tea, Charlie's restaurant and the Donovan Bar
best_for: Travelers drawn to literary and royal history

facts.text: Brown's Hotel is in London's Mayfair.
Brown's Hotel has welcomed guests in Mayfair since 1832.
The hotel's founder was Sarah Brown.
The Drawing Room keeps its original wood panelling.
The Drawing Room serves breakfast, dinner and afternoon tea.
Charlie's restaurant is named after Lord Charles Forte.
The Donovan Bar's cocktail menu is by Salvatore Calabrese and Director of Mixology Federico Pavan.
The Donovan Bar has a corner called The Naughty Corner.
Forte Suites include in-suite check-in and complimentary breakfast.
The Three-Bedroom Paul Smith Grand Suite reflects Sir Paul Smith's signature style.
The spa uses Irene Forte Skincare for its signature treatments.
Dogs staying at the hotel get bedding from a William Morris At Home partnership.

highlights.text: Rudyard Kipling wrote The Jungle Book at Brown's Hotel, and the Kipling Suite is named after him.
Queen Victoria liked to take her afternoon tea at Brown's, in the Drawing Room.
The Donovan Bar celebrates fashion photographer Terence Donovan.
Every Thursday evening the Drawing Room hosts live jazz performances by leading London musicians.
At Charlie's, roast beef and venison en croute are carved tableside from a trolley.

considerations.text: The spa is small, with three treatment rooms.
The Donovan Bar asks guests not to wear sportswear or shorts.
WhataHotel notes the traditional decor may feel dated to some modern travelers.
